title: How many steps would a ladder to the Moon have?
description: A ladder to the Moon has steps twenty centimetres apart, and the Moon is 384400 kilometres away. We change kilometres to centimetres and divide to count the steps. The result is compared with folding paper, where each fold doubles the thickness.
teaching_notes: One idea: put both lengths in the same unit before dividing to count steps. Watch for students who divide kilometres by centimetres directly.

source: How many 20 cm steps would a ladder to the Moon, 384400 km away, have?
video_script.why: To count equal steps in a long distance, both lengths must be in the same unit; the same fixed gain at every step is linear growth, unlike doubling.
video_script.substitution: Change kilometres to centimetres, then divide the distance by the height of one step.
video_script.anchor: a ladder to the Moon with steps of 20 cm, against folding paper
video_script.wrong_answer: nineteen thousand two hundred twenty steps
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko divides 384400 km by 20 cm as plain numbers and gets 19220 steps. The units differ: 384400 km is 38440000000 cm, so the true count is 1922000000.
video_script.payoff_line: Put both lengths in the same unit, then divide to count the steps

final_answer.value: 1922000000 steps, about 192 crore, against just 46 folds
final_answer.spoken: The ladder needs about one hundred ninety two crore steps. Folding paper takes only forty six folds.
